findings: Hardcoded modal detail labels — DriverDetail, PassengerDetail, and TripDetail all use plain English string literals as row labels ('Name', 'License #', 'Account Status', 'Vehicle Type', 'Trip ID', 'Passenger Phone', etc.) instead of t() calls. Roughly 40 visible strings bypass i18n entirely. Replace each literal with a t('th_...') or a dedicated key.

Hardcoded status options in Trips filter — The <select> in Trips.tsx (lines 122–126) uses bare English option text ('Pending', 'Accepted', 'In Progress', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'). The cancel button tooltip at line 277 ('Trip is already in a terminal state') is also hardcoded. Replace with t('status_...') keys that already exist in i18n.ts.

PostgreSQL rejects NaN parameters with a type error and the catch block returns 500. Add isNaN guards and fall back to defaults (50 and 0).
